title: field read-redaction — `mask unless` crossed with `audited` (two masked fields + a masked contained part, projected twice in one scope)
note: the CROSSING is the point: an audited op renders the masked projection twice into one method body, which is where a fixed principal-variable name collides (.NET CS0128)

apiCaller.//: The same entity-history read class: `field-mask` reads its audited aggregate's trail as the unprivileged principal (the masked-field DROP and the RS-45 `actor`).

authzGate.//: The audit-history read projects the same masked shape (`historyFind` copies the list read's gate at enrichment), so it inherits the mask.

//: The CONTROL rung — the arm that keeps every 403 above honest (M-T9.28 slice 2).

Every other entry in this map asserts that the unauthorized principal is REFUSED.  None of them can tell "the gate denied" from "this identity is refused everywhere": if the dev-stub verifier ever began answering 403 for an unrecognised role, every `unauthorized: 403` arm in `auth-simple`, `auth-oidc`, `read-gates` and `lifecycle-guard` would stay green while proving nothing about any gate.  Only an UNGATED surface answering 2xx to that same identity closes it, and until this entry there was none.

`field-mask` is the right host: it declares `auth: required` (so the second identity is expressible) and carries NO `requires`, `policy` or tenancy predicate at all — its one authorization surface is the read mask, which redacts a FIELD inside a 200 rather than refusing the request.  So the arm doubles as that mask's second-identity witness: the RECORDED body must still carry `salary` and `nationalId` as null, because neither harness principal holds `people.unmask` (deliberate — see the fixture).  A backend that keyed the mask on "is there a principal at all" instead of on the permission leaks here and nowhere else.

The visibility taint's sinks (docs/auth.md).  Neither harness principal holds `people.unmask`, so both are refused; the control beside them is the same route answering 204 when the masked keys are left out — the refusal is the mask's, not the identity's.

gated.label: control — ungated read, so the second identity must NOT be refused
mask write gate — a new value for a masked field is refused
control — the same update without the masked keys goes through
mask read gate — a lookup filtering on a masked field is refused
